contradicted: The dispatch's premise that this defect is a WRONG ADDRESS is confirmed; the dispatch's implied remedy -- fix the address and the cost becomes measurable -- is CONTRADICTED by three live measurements this lane made. (1) run.googleapis.com/job/billable_instance_time, the metric compute-cost.mjs reads, DOES NOT EXIST in project hauska-prod-497015: the Monitoring API answers HTTP 404 'Cannot find metric(s) that match type = "run.googleapis.com/job/billable_instance_time"', and the project's only run.googleapis.com/job/* descriptors are completed_execution_count, completed_task_attempt_count, running_executions, running_task_attempts (the job's own sibling canaries are counted, never its instance-seconds). The nearest real metric, run.googleapis.com/container/billable_instance_time, reports 0.1 instance-seconds for the same execution window the module's fallback prices at 30.7 seconds -- a 300x difference, i.e. a different quantity, not a misspelling. (2) NO production caller injects deps.monitoringFn (grep: monitoringFn appears only in test files), so readBillableInstanceSeconds returns BILLABLE_TIME_UNAVAILABLE: why=no monitoring reader injected WITHOUT making any request -- today the billed quantity is never read in production at all. (3) instanceShapeFromExecution cannot read the v1 body that this client's own gcloud fallback returns (INSTANCE_SHAPE_UNAVAILABLE {missing: cpu}), while the direct v2 body parses correctly. Consequence stated plainly: with this fix merged, the reaper will still write execution-window figures, not billed ones -- but they will be correct-JOB window figures, and each row will now name the failed metric read instead of reading as a transport failure. Choosing which quantity is 'the compute cost' is returned as leave_behind #1, not decided here.
contradictedAlso: The dispatch's line 'a job cannot read its own final billable time while it runs (METRIC_NOT_YET_PUBLISHED)' is a consequence of reading the wrong metric: METRIC_NOT_YET_PUBLISHED is what the module returns when the metric set is empty, and for this project it is empty for every window, not only while the job runs.
missionPremise: P-284 merged at afdda42 (migration 0012 applied, the setback writer image rebuilt, the Caldwell dry run factory-parcel-setback-cells-x9zmt writing a stage record) and its compute cost reads BILLABLE_TIME_UNAVAILABLE: why=execution describe failed. The dispatch's finding (integration seat, 2026-09-16, proven both ways) is that a Cloud Run execution's resource name is jobs/<job>/executions/<name>, that getExecution's job parameter defaults to the remembered factory-atoms-cad, and that both cost lookups therefore addressed a different job; the 404 that comes back is indistinguishable from a transport failure. scratch._purpose: FLEET MEMORY (M0) block: LESSON / DEAD-END / GROUND-TRUTH / OPEN entries, returned for the planner to gate. Promotion is the planner's call, not this lane's.
LESSON: A wrong resource name and a transport failure are the SAME observation at the call site: both arrive as a failed fetch. That is why the refusal (JOB_NOT_NAMED, before any request) is worth more than a better error message after the fact -- a call site that FALLS to a default while holding a different identity cannot be distinguished from one that was never given the identity, unless it refuses.

A default parameter that is correct for its current callers is still a hazard for the NEXT caller: getExecution's jobName default is right for both atoms-cad loops and produced a silent 404 for every other job the moment a second job reused it. The place to state that is the caller list, not the parameter.

A fallback figure and a measured figure that look identical on the row are the SILENT FALLBACK defect class; the fix is not to remove the fallback but to write the reason for it into the same basis the number travels in.

A dry run cannot be costed by anything that keys on a `runs` row: the record must carry its own execution identity, because for a dry run there is no other place it can live. Any telemetry column shaped 'run_id->run->scope' silently excludes the case the metering program most wants to read.

A test that asserts a URL CONTAINS the execution name proves nothing about the job -- the execution name is in the URL under every job. The assertion that can only pass on correct code is an INEQUALITY against the wrong address.
DEAD-END: Reconstructing the job from the execution name (Cloud Run execution names START with the job name) works today and breaks the day a job is renamed with a stale execution in the window; rejected in CP1 as a guess, and the identity is READ instead.
Storing the identity as a JSONB blob on the record: two named columns can be indexed and read back by name; a blob is a third shape of 'execution identity' in the repo and cannot be constrained.
Reading billable_instance_time alone without the execution describe: the metric is instance-SECONDS and only the execution carries the vCPU/memory shape that turns seconds into dollars.

Passing the job down from every stage writer: it would have required editing src/jobs/parcel-setback-cells.mjs, held by the open P-256 lane, and would make every future writer responsible for remembering its job -- the drift the stage-completeness test exists to stop. Stamping it inside openStageRun from the writer's own env needs no job file at all.

gcloud run jobs executions describe with a --job flag: this gcloud version has no such flag (the job is meant to be part of the execution argument); the v2 REST path with an access token is what both measured the 200/404 pair and what the module itself uses.
